reasoning: Ratchet the Airbus gain floor from €201 to €205. The base has walked up — the last low of consequence is €206.30 on 3 August and every close since is €210 or better — so €201 sits under the 31 July low, which is history now. €205 books +18.2% on my €173.46 entry, keeps three shares on a confirmed delivery cycle, and deliberately stops short of the €210.90 seven-session low: a floor tucked under one week of consolidation is a whipsaw, not a rail. Same correction I made at SU €284→€294.

Pre-draw the add I said I had room for when I opened this starter at €170.32: €164 is the middle of the €160–171 shelf Air Liquide spent April through June building, not a level invented from today's chart. Eight down closes on volume shrinking from 732k to 470k is the defensive sleeve being sold to fund the industrial melt-up — take-or-pay contracts, four decades of dividend growth, D/E ~0.5 and a P/E inside my 30 cap have not moved. Sized to one share (~€165 with fees) so it and my standing €128.70 Legrand bid for 3 (~€387) both clear €559 of cash even if they fire the same day.

ThyssenKrupp is the only expanding-volume thrust on the STOXX 600 board. Ten sessions coiled 12.03-12.60 on 0.62-1.13x, then 08/13 opens 12.05, runs to 13.52 and closes AT the high, +9.03% on 5,469,994 shares — 2.50x the 60-day average and the heaviest print in the series — clearing the 13.195 52-week-high close outright. 3m RS +21.6pp and 6m +141.1pp over VGK. One day is a candle, not a trend, so it does not get a market order: buy-stop at 13.70 sits above the 13.52 high so it fills on continuation or never. 165 shares is 2,261 EUR, 22.4% of my 10,077 NAV, inside the 25% cap even on a 15.00 gap-through. Quotes in EUR, no FX leg.

Same thesis, corrected level. The 08/12 gap from 39.80 to 42.08 was an earnings beat with raised guidance and net profit up 30%, closing 41.79 on 3,136,226 shares — 1.56x and the heaviest tape in the series — with 3m RS +21.6pp and 6m +206.6pp over VGK, best in the bank complex. But 08/13 printed a 42.67 high and closed 41.50 at the low of the day on 1.17x, which puts my old 42.55 stop underneath the range high where it fires on a wick rather than on continuation. 42.80 clears the 42.67 outright. 56 shares is 2,397 EUR, 23.8% of NAV, inside the cap even on a 44.50 gap-through.

Cut the position whose thesis was factually wrong, at market, not at the leash. I bought this calling $505.18 a fresh 52-week high; the actual 52-week high is $553.72 set 2025-10-28, and at $495.40 the stock sits -10.5% below it while SWK, CPAY, CRL and MPC are all within 3% of theirs. That makes it a recovery name in a momentum book, and RS +17.2pp over three months and +9.6pp over six is the weakest pair I hold. It is not breaking — 16.2M shares on 8/14 is the lightest volume of the entire advance and by my own rule a dry-up earns a leash — but a leash is for a leader digesting, and this was never a leader. Selling on a bad thesis rather than a bad print is the difference between the RTX lesson and repeating it. Books -0.9% from my $499.99 entry on 19.3% of the book and funds a name that is actually at a high.

The cleanest thing left on a narrowing board. Five consecutive higher closes — 314.01, 321.07, 325.57, 328.31, 332.69 — closing at 0.96, 0.68, 0.72, 0.88 and 0.90 of their ranges, into a fresh 52-week high $333.24 with the close $0.55 under it, on volume 1.36/1.42/1.63/0.83/1.33M against a 1.58M average. Steady-to-declining volume at the highs is the same continuation structure MPC gave me, and unlike MPC this one leads on both windows: RS +49.4pp over three months and +42.6pp over six against SPY. On a session where 19 names made new highs and most were sold into the close, EXPE finished at 0.90 of range — relative strength on a tired tape is the only signal I trade. 7 shares at ~$332.69 = ~$2,329, 18.2% of book, inside my 25% cap, funded by the MSFT sale with ~$626 to spare so a gap-up open cannot reject the fill.

Opening leash on the new slot at $318. The five-session run has built higher lows at 304.20, 310.91, 316.09, 318.85 and 327.88, so $318 sits under the 8/13 low 318.85 and under the 8/12 close 325.57 — a close there gives back 8/13 and 8/14 in full and puts price back inside the 316-325 shelf it broke out of, which is the honest invalidation rather than a round number. Risk -4.4% from entry, well inside my -10% rule and deliberately not tighter: a name that has advanced five sessions straight can take one 3% day and be perfectly healthy, and equity triggers settle on the close.

Fourth peel, at market, and I am done pretending otherwise: my upside rungs have never fired in three peels and BTC will not resolve my cap on strength. It is the single broken thing I own — 14% of its 45-day range against SPY at 97%, gold at 93%, CL2.PA at 90% — and still 42% of book against a 35% cap. 0.02 takes it to 30.3%, decisively inside the cap with room for the book itself to move, and leaves 0.05 that both re-cut ladders mirror whole.

Rotate the broken leg of the debasement trade into the working one. Gold is +8.2% in ten sessions and 93% of its 45-day range while BTC is -2.5% and 14%; both are the same monetary bid, only one is being paid for it. The 08-13 red candle I refused to buy has now held for three sessions at 121.83, so this is an add into a consolidation, not into a first down day. Twenty shares is €2,437 = 27% of book, inside the 35% cap, funded from €2,028 cash on hand before the peel even settles.

Repair authored at the same moment as the add, not a session later. The armed stop covers 10 of what will be 20 shares — bit for bit the CL2.PA bug that left 40 of 60 naked and that I only caught on the second pass. €113.50 stays the level, still under the €113.90 close of 08-04, the candle before the breakout, so it fires only if the entire run has failed; it now exits the whole leg. Risks ~€168 on a €121.92 blend instead of the €488 my -20% mandate stop would wear.

Re-cut of the €56,400 rung from 0.04 to 0.02 so the upside ladder totals the 0.05 I will actually hold. Level unchanged — it sits €132 under the €56,532 high printed on 08-10, a price this tape has genuinely traded — and stacked under the 0.03 @ €55,800 rung it still takes BTC from 30% of book to zero on a single green day. The size is arithmetic, not conviction: 0.03 + 0.02 = 0.05, and the mirror is what keeps the last leg from dying on INSUFFICIENT_SHARES.

Downside mirror re-cut to match: 0.03 @ €53,700 plus 0.02 @ €48,750 totals the 0.05 held. €53,700 remains a true break level — every sub-€53,700 print in the window is early July, and the closest test since is the €53,959 low of 08-14, €259 above it — so the €48,750 mandate stop stays what it has always been, the tranche that catches the move that keeps going after the break rung has already halved me.

The fifth line, and deliberately non-refiner. Memory/storage is the only coherent group move on the board besides the one I already own twice, and STX is the leveraged expression with real liquidity ($5.1bn of daily notional). Three consecutive closes above the prior day's high out of a 760-890 base, each closing near the high, on volume expanding 3.2M to 5.2M, with an unfilled gap from Thursday's 934.77 high to Friday's 941.26 open. I take it over MU (+11%, cleaner but half the amplitude) because my mandate is the leveraged expression, and over WDC, which is still 10% below its pre-8/06 level and is therefore the laggard, not the leader. 2 x 973.44 = $1,946.88 against $3,940.73 of cash — 16.7% of NAV, inside the 30% order cap ($3,495) and my 35% position cap, and it deliberately leaves $1,993 so the pending NEM add at 120.25 can still fill rather than rejecting on cash.

Stop armed the same session I buy the line — permanent rule, no naked positions. 895 sits just above the 885 shelf the breakout cleared and 1.1 daily ranges below Friday's 920.00 low, so it fires only if the entire three-day breakout is given back, not on one violent open in a name with 70-point ranges. Risk 973.44 to 895 = $78.44 x 2 = $157, 1.35% of NAV; that is -8.1%, comfortably tighter than my -20% disaster rule, which is a ceiling and not a target. $1,790 of notional, trivially inside the cap.

Ratchet from 330, which is now 7.2% below the market on a stock that has run +19.4% in five sessions — that is not a stop, that is a spectator. 342 sits under the 8/13 low of 344.00 and about 1.4 daily ranges below Friday's 352.48 low, so it survives a normal 4%-a-day session and fires on a genuine unwind. Friday was the first close off the high of the whole run (360.10 high, 355.42 close) while crude rose — one rest day, not a break, but a parabola is exactly where the stop has to lead the price. Floor improves from -$128 to -$44 against my 348.25 cost; still under water, which is correct, because the stop follows the tape and not what I paid. $2,394 of notional, inside the ~$3,495 cap.

Ratchet from 318, same reasoning as MPC and looser by design because VLO is 4.9pp less extended. 325 sits under the 8/13 low of 326.12 and about 1.5 daily ranges below Friday's 339.23 low, so it clears a full retest of Thursday's range before it fires. Deliberately wider in percentage terms than MPC's 342 (4.9% vs 3.8%): the more extended name gets the tighter leash, which is the only sensible way to hold the same trade twice. Floor improves from -$149 to -$107 against my 342.92 cost. $1,950 of notional, inside the cap.

Close the full Sika line at market, ~190.85, +1.9% on the 187.25 cost. The thesis was momentum — six consecutive higher closes since the 07-28 re-rating gap, corroborated by Saint-Gobain +9.8% the same session — and that structure has been gone for seven sessions: 195.50 on 08-05 then 191.30, 194.00, 193.55, 193.55, 193.10, 191.15, 190.85, a slow bleed with no new high while every other name in this book printed one. Exiting on falsification before the 186.00 rail fires is the same discipline that got me out of XLU, XLV and AAPL. FX stance: booked in francs, and cutting CHF from 20% to 8% of book is the point — the franc sleeve was my second-largest currency behind sterling on the strength of a chart that stopped working, and a haven currency is not a reason to hold a fading asset.

Chevron at 200.00 gapped 186.56 to 194.91 on 08-10 with crude reclaiming 82, then printed 196.66, 196.60, 197.70, 200.00 — four higher closes holding the gap on falling volume, the same hold-the-gap shape that made Airbus work — inside a sector where XLE, XOM and COP all sit at 60-day highs, so this is breadth rather than a single chart, the test I applied to the European banks. Energy is the one macro theme absent from a book that is otherwise banks, defence, bullion, crypto and diagnostics, and a crude recovery supports rather than contradicts the rising-term-premium trade I already own. Sized at 7 shares, ~1,210 EUR, 11.8% of book, inside my 20% cap. FX stance: deliberately dollar, lifting USD from 7.5% to 19.3% and cutting the home sleeve nothing while the franc pays for it — a euro stalled at 1.1573 after failing at 1.1556 twice makes translation neutral, and unlike Airbus an oil major has no strong-euro headwind buried in its earnings.

Protective stop on the new dollar energy line at 193.50, beneath the 194.91 close of the 08-10 gap day and above the 192.31 close of 07-30, so it is not resting on a visited close. This is a gap entry and my own rule gives a gap the tighter leash — Airbus and Intesa both got it — so -3.25% from 200.00 marks where the gap has begun to fill and the crude recovery that is the entire thesis is being given back, rather than where I get nervous. FX stance: written in dollars, so a firming euro stops me in USD and compounds the loss in EUR rather than cushioning it — the honest cost of a dollar line in a euro book, and the reason the stop is tight rather than the position small.

Ratchet the Intesa rail from 6.65 to 6.77. The name has ground 6.797 to 6.917 over seven sessions with no close under 6.797 and a fresh high yesterday, so a level set beneath my 6.696 entry is history rather than risk management. 6.77 sits under the 6.797 close that forms the base of this advance, is not on a visited close, and converts a -3.9% defensive stop into a -2.1% one that also books a small gain — the gap-entry-gets-the-tighter-leash rule still governing the line it was written for. FX stance: EUR in, EUR out, no currency leg.

Ratchet the BAE rail from 21.30 to 21.90. Since that level was written the name has held 22.44, 22.30, 22.70, 22.36, 22.58 and made a new high, so 21.30 now sits two shelves below the live structure. 21.90 is beneath the 22.00 close of 08-06 that is the floor of the current leg and above the 21.56 pullback close, without resting on a visited close, cutting risk from -5.7% to -3.0% of spot while still marking where a sixteen-session grind is dead rather than where I get nervous. FX stance: written in pounds, so a firming sterling stops me in GBP but lands me softer in EUR — the currency leg cushions the asset leg, which is why the defence sleeve is denominated here.

Ratchet the Julius Baer rail from 71.00 to 73.50. The grind has extended two more sessions to a fresh 75.80 high, so a -6.3% leash written at entry is now three legs below the live structure. 73.50 sits beneath the 74.02 and 74.16 closes of 05 and 06 August that form the base of the final leg and above the 71.78 shelf, is not on a visited close, and cuts risk from -6.3% to -3.0% — about three average daily ranges for a name that moves roughly 1% a day, so it is a rail and not a tripwire. It also now guards my only franc line rather than one of two. FX stance: set in francs, so a firming franc stops me in CHF but lands me softer in EUR; the currency leg still cushions the asset leg, which is why the last 8% of CHF stays rather than following Sika out.
